prompt.context: You are the CEO of American Airlines. You are just informed that the price of oil has dropped to nearly $0. Basically, consider the idea that you can acquire oil as easily as you could water. Assume that there are no significant costs in transporting the oil, acquiring it, etc.
prompt.question: Who are the first three people you would call within your organization as the CEO? Explain your motivations for contacting each of these people and what you hope to accomplish just having received this information about the price of oil.

clarifying_info.q: Would competitor airlines have access to the same low-cost fuel?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, competitors would have access to the same low-cost fuel.

framework: Identify how fuel/oil costs fit into the overall cost structure and P&L
Assess competitive implications — since all airlines face the same fuel cost drop, pricing strategy must account for potential price wars
Evaluate demand side: routes, capacity, and consumer preferences
Consider operational changes: new routes, short-haul expansion, direct vs. indirect flight mix
Think about strategic differentiation beyond price

questions.prompt: Name and explain the rationale for each of the three people you would call.
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify CFO (cost structure and financial impact), Marketing (demand and pricing opportunity), and Operations/Scheduling (capacity and route changes). Each contact should have a clear purpose tied to acting on the new cost reality. Candidates should proactively note the risk of a price war given that competitors share the same fuel cost advantage.

questions.prompt: Interviewer follow-up: You mentioned lowering prices, but competitors can also lower their prices. You could get into a price war that depletes revenues. Are you sure about this? What else might you consider?
questions.guidance: Strong answer pivots from pure price competition to differentiation. Key ideas: (1) Use Chicago hub advantage — AA offers all-direct flights out of Chicago, which is a major hub; lower fuel costs now allow AA to price direct flights competitively against indirect competitor flights at comparable or lower fares while still delivering premium convenience. (2) Explore Southwest-style short-haul expansion — with near-zero fuel costs, very short routes (e.g., Chicago to Detroit) become economical, competing with driving and other transport modes. Candidate should demonstrate awareness that the value proposition shifts from cost to service quality and convenience.

brainstorming.prompt: What strategic opportunities does near-zero fuel cost create for American Airlines?

categories.name: Cost Structure
ideas: Lower cost per flight, potentially moving loss-making routes to breakeven or profit
Re-examine fleet decisions: larger, less fuel-efficient planes may now be viable
Reduce or eliminate fuel surcharges passed to passengers

categories.name: Pricing Strategy
ideas: Lower fares selectively to gain market share without triggering a full price war
Price direct flights at parity with competitors' indirect fares to win price-sensitive travelers
Avoid race-to-the-bottom by leading with value (direct flights, hub convenience) not just price

categories.name: Route Expansion
ideas: Add direct long-haul routes that were previously uneconomical
Launch short-haul routes competing with driving (Chicago-Detroit, Chicago-Milwaukee)
Increase flight frequency on existing routes to capture more demand

categories.name: Competitive Differentiation
ideas: Leverage Chicago hub status for maximum direct-flight coverage
Emphasize direct flights as a premium yet now affordable product
Invest cost savings into service quality improvements to build brand loyalty

categories.name: Operational / Capacity
ideas: Increase overall capacity (more flights per day) to drive revenue growth
Use freed-up budget to accelerate fleet modernization or maintenance
Evaluate whether previously grounded aircraft become economical to operate

recommendation: Call the CFO first to quantify the cost savings per flight and identify which routes or segments shift from loss-making to profitable with near-zero fuel costs.
Call the Marketing Department to understand demand elasticity and identify which routes or markets present the best opportunity to grow revenue through competitive pricing or new offerings.
Call the Scheduler/Operations head to translate financial and demand insights into specific capacity and route changes, particularly short-haul expansion and increased direct-flight frequency.
risks: All competitors gain the same fuel cost advantage, so price cuts alone will not create durable competitive advantage and may trigger destructive price wars.
Near-zero oil is a hypothetical extreme scenario; strategy should be pressure-tested against what happens if fuel costs normalize.
Rapid capacity expansion could outpace demand, leading to low load factors and revenue dilution.
next_steps: Model contribution margin by route under the new fuel cost assumption to prioritize which routes to expand or reprice first.
Conduct customer research on willingness to pay for direct flights vs. indirect flights at various price points.
Develop a competitive response playbook in case major rivals move aggressively on price before AA can differentiate on service.
